hypothesis: Separating training from the target scope—using the public reference's larger training scope 152 and 100 bounded training trials—will produce a usable Gaussian mark model and allow the bit-parallel reversible-deletion search to test scope 111.
rationale: The first adapted reference run used TRAINING_M=111 and spent 120 seconds without completing a training trial, so its main search was never exercised. The public source itself uses a larger training scope than its target; restoring that separation is a principled runtime adaptation, not a target change.
expected_information_gain: Determines whether the FPGA-reference search family can reach main-phase target search under software execution once its training distribution is learned from an easier finite scope.
method: Read the pinned public dts-search-hdl source at commit 2ccff8e767c3fe6390fd3af056dfda11847011fc. In a temporary build file, adapt n=14,k=4,M=146 to n=7,k=5,M=111, retain bit-parallel spectrum checks, Gaussian mark sampling, reversible row deletion, and deterministic seed 20260902, but set TRAINING_M=152 and TRAINING_TRIALS=100. Compile with WSL gcc -Wall -Ofast and run for 120 seconds. Parse any decoded rows and independently validate them with the repository integer verifier.
metric: training completions, decoded candidate, independent DTS validity, scope, main-phase entry, and runtime
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A verifier-valid decoded seven-row assignment with scope<=111 is exactly a true-objective witness; training completion and partial output are diagnostics only.
kill_condition: Stop at the first independently validated scope-111 witness or after 120 seconds; preserve complete stdout/stderr and transformed-source hashes. Do not infer infeasibility from timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and validator-valid

previous_best_comparison.fpga_reference_001: training_M=111 produced no completed training trial in 120 seconds
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: same external bit-parallel algorithm with source-faithful larger training scope

interpretation: The public FPGA-reference algorithm reached its main target search after successful separated training, but all observed target trials stalled at six populated rows within 120 seconds. No candidate was decoded or verified.
what_was_learned: The training bottleneck was removed; the limiting event is now seventh-row completion under the source's default block-attempt and DTS-generation thresholds. This is finite runtime evidence, not a global negative result.
recommended_next_action: Run one threshold variant increasing block-generation attempts and DTS-generation iterations, retaining all other source behavior; if no seventh-row completion occurs, pause this software route pending hardware-scale search.
repetition_justification: This changes a theoretically necessary training condition identified by the previous failure: training is conducted at the public algorithm's larger scope and bounded trials, while target M, algorithm, seed, and verifier remain fixed.
